SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

throw verb

also toss

classical

jaciō, jacere

verb, third conjugation

Examples

  • Pilam mihi jace.

    Throw me the ball.composed

  • pater eam lēniter conjiciēbat, Theodōrus manibus excipiēbat, aut, sī ēlāpsa erat, pede ad patrem pulsābat

    Dad tossed it gently, Theo caught it in his hands or, if it slipped, kicked it back to DadLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

  • Ibi follem, quem puerī quīdam pede pulsābant, ad sē volūtum Theodōrus ambābus manibus ad eōs conjēcit.

    There some boys were kicking a ball; when it rolled to him Theo threw it back to them with both hands.Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

Other words

  • conjiciō, conjicere, conjēcī, conjectum — throw, toss

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 44: pilam conjicere

See also catch, kick, ball.

SourcesLewis & Short: conicio

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 44, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).

Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
